questions.question: In an open queueing network of $M$ stations with external arrival rates $\gamma_i$ and routing probabilities $P_{ij}$, the traffic equations are written for unknown rates $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_M$. What does $\lambda_i$ denote?
options: The rate at which new jobs enter station $i$ from outside the network.
The total arrival rate at station $i$: external jobs plus jobs routed from all stations.
The rate at which jobs leave the network directly after service at station $i$.
The rate at which station $i$ can complete jobs when its server is never idle.

questions.question: In the traffic equations $\lambda_i=\gamma_i+\sum_{j=1}^M\lambda_jP_{ji}$ of an open network, the flow from station $j$ to station $i$ is written as $\lambda_jP_{ji}$, where $\lambda_j$ is the arrival rate at $j$. Which assumption justifies using the arrival rate $\lambda_j$ rather than the departure rate $\delta_j$ of station $j$?
options: External arrivals form a Poisson process, so every internal stream is Poisson as well.
Every station serves its jobs in first-come-first-served order of arrival.
Every station is rate stable, so its departure rate $\delta_j$ equals $\lambda_j$.
Every station has a single server, so it completes its jobs one at a time.

questions.question: A student claims that the traffic equations $\lambda_i=\gamma_i+\sum_{j=1}^M\lambda_jP_{ji}$ of an open network hold only when external arrivals are Poisson and all service times are exponential. Which assessment of this claim is correct?
options: The claim is false: rate stability and Markov routing suffice, for any distributions.
The claim is true: only Poisson streams can be split by routing probabilities.
The claim is true: rates of merged streams add up only when the streams are Poisson.
The claim is false, but routing must be deterministic, with every $P_{ji}$ equal to 0 or 1.

questions.question: In the traffic equations $\lambda_i=\gamma_i+\sum_{j=1}^M\lambda_jP_{ji}$ of an open network, the sum also contains the term with $j=i$, namely $\lambda_iP_{ii}$. What does this term account for?
options: Jobs that wait in the queue of station $i$ before their first service there.
Jobs that leave the network right after their service at station $i$.
External jobs that arrive at station $i$ and are counted a second time.
Jobs that finish service at station $i$ and are routed straight back to $i$.

questions.question: In an open network of rate-stable stations with external rates $\gamma_i$, the long-run rate at which jobs leave the network is $\sum_{i=1}^M\lambda_iP_{i0}$, where $P_{i0}$ is the probability of leaving after service at $i$. What does this sum equal?
options: The sum of all station arrival rates $\sum_{i=1}^M\lambda_i$, as each station releases $\lambda_i$.
The total external arrival rate $|\boldsymbol{\gamma}|=\sum_{i=1}^M\gamma_i$, with or without feedback.
The total external rate $|\boldsymbol{\gamma}|$ only without feedback; with feedback it is larger.
The largest station arrival rate $\max_i\lambda_i$, which is set by the busiest station.

questions.question: An open network has two stations. External jobs arrive only at station 1, at rate $\gamma_1=3$ per hour. The routing probabilities are $P_{11}=0.1$, $P_{12}=0.6$, $P_{21}=0.3$ and $P_{22}=0.2$. Which equation is the traffic equation for $\lambda_2$?
options: $\lambda_2=0.3\lambda_1+0.2\lambda_2$
$\lambda_2=3+0.6\lambda_1+0.2\lambda_2$
$\lambda_2=0.6\lambda_1+0.2\lambda_2$
$\lambda_2=0.6\lambda_1$

questions.question: A tandem line has four stations. All external jobs enter at station 1 at rate $\gamma_1=5$ per hour, $P_{i,i+1}=1$ for $i=1,2,3$, and every job leaves after station 4. All stations are rate stable. What is the arrival rate $\lambda_4$ at station 4?
options: $\lambda_4=20$ jobs per hour
$\lambda_4=1.25$ jobs per hour
$\lambda_4=0$ jobs per hour
$\lambda_4=5$ jobs per hour

questions.question: In an open network, station 2 has arrival rate $\lambda_2=5$ jobs per hour and is rate stable. After service there a job goes to station 1 with probability $P_{21}=0.3$, back to station 2 with $P_{22}=0.1$, to station 3 with $P_{23}=0.2$, and otherwise leaves the network. At what rate do jobs leave the network from station 2?
options: 2 exits per hour
3 exits per hour
2.5 exits per hour
5 exits per hour

questions.question: In an open network, jobs arrive from outside at station 1 at rate $\gamma_1=6$ per hour and at station 2 at rate $\gamma_2=1$ per hour. After station 1 a job goes to station 2 with probability $\tfrac{1}{3}$ and to station 3 with probability $\tfrac{2}{3}$; station 2 sends all its jobs to station 3, and after station 3 every job leaves the network. All stations are rate stable. What is $\lambda_2$?
options: $\lambda_2=2$ per hour
$\lambda_2=3$ per hour
$\lambda_2=5$ per hour
$\lambda_2=7$ per hour

questions.question: A network with one station receives external jobs at rate $\gamma=4$ per hour. After each service, independently, a job needs rework with probability $P_{11}=0.2$ and rejoins the same queue; otherwise it leaves. The station is rate stable. What is its total arrival rate $\lambda_1$?
options: $\lambda_1=4$ per hour
$\lambda_1=4.8$ per hour
$\lambda_1=20$ per hour
$\lambda_1=5$ per hour

questions.question: An open network has feedback, so some jobs revisit stations, and its total external arrival rate is $|\boldsymbol{\gamma}|=\sum_i\gamma_i$. Can the arrival rate $\lambda_i$ that solves the traffic equations exceed $|\boldsymbol{\gamma}|$ while every station is rate stable?
options: Yes: a job may visit station $i$ several times, and $\lambda_i/|\boldsymbol{\gamma}|$ is its mean number of visits.
No: each job enters the network once, so flow conservation forces $\lambda_i\leq|\boldsymbol{\gamma}|$ at each station.
Yes, but only when station $i$ is overloaded, so that its arriving jobs pile up there.
Yes, but only when station $i$ itself has external arrivals, that is when $\gamma_i>0$.

questions.question: An open network has a fixed routing matrix $\boldsymbol{P}$ for which $\boldsymbol{I}-\boldsymbol{P}$ is invertible, so the traffic equations have a unique solution $\boldsymbol{\lambda}$. If every external rate $\gamma_i$ is doubled and $\boldsymbol{P}$ stays the same, what happens to $\boldsymbol{\lambda}$?
options: Each $\lambda_i$ grows by $\gamma_i$, so stations without external arrivals keep their rate.
Each $\lambda_i$ more than doubles at stations on a feedback loop, since returns compound.
Each $\lambda_i$ doubles, including at stations that receive no external arrivals.
Each $\lambda_i$ doubles only in a tandem line; with feedback the change is nonlinear.

questions.question: For an open network of single-server stations with mean service times $\mathbb{E}[S_i]$, the traffic equations have a unique nonnegative solution $\boldsymbol{\lambda}$. What must still be checked before the $\lambda_i$ can be taken as the actual long-run arrival rates?
options: Nothing more: a nonnegative solution already shows that every station is rate stable.
That $\rho_i=\lambda_i\mathbb{E}[S_i]<1$ holds at every station $i=1,\ldots,M$.
That the network output $\sum_{i=1}^M\lambda_iP_{i0}$ equals the external rate $|\boldsymbol{\gamma}|$.
That $\gamma_i\mathbb{E}[S_i]<1$ holds at every station that has external arrivals.

questions.question: Two stations form an open network. External jobs arrive only at station 1, at rate $\gamma=3$ per hour. The routing probabilities are $P_{11}=0.2$, $P_{12}=0.8$, $P_{21}=0.3$ and $P_{22}=0.4$, and jobs leave after station 2 with probability $0.3$. Assuming rate stability, what is $\lambda_2$?
options: $\lambda_2=3.75$ per hour
$\lambda_2=5$ per hour
$\lambda_2=3$ per hour
$\lambda_2=10$ per hour

questions.question: Station 1 of an open network has $c_1=4$ parallel servers with mean service time $\mathbb{E}[S_1]=0.3$ hours. External jobs arrive at station 1 at rate 9 per hour. After station 1 a job goes to station 2 with probability 0.5 or leaves; after station 2 it returns to station 1 with probability 0.2 or leaves. What is the load $\lambda_1\mathbb{E}[S_1]/c_1$ of station 1?

An open network has two stations. External jobs arrive only at station 1, at rate 7 per hour. After station 1 a job goes to station 2 with probability 0.5 or leaves; after station 2 it returns to station 1 with probability 0.25 or leaves. All stations are rate stable. What fraction of the jobs leaving the network leave from station 2?

In a two-station open network, external jobs arrive at station 1 at rate $\gamma_1>0$, and every row of the routing matrix $\boldsymbol{P}$ sums to one, so $P_{10}=P_{20}=0$ and no job ever leaves. What can be said about the traffic equations $\lambda_i=\gamma_i+\sum_{j}\lambda_jP_{ji}$?
options: They have the unique solution $\boldsymbol{\lambda}=\boldsymbol{\gamma}(\boldsymbol{I}-\boldsymbol{P})^{-1}$, as for any routing matrix.
They have infinitely many solutions; one is fixed by requiring $\lambda_1+\lambda_2=\gamma_1$.
They have a solution only when every service is fast enough that each $\rho_i<1$.
They have no solution, since summing them would force $\gamma_1=\sum_i\lambda_iP_{i0}=0$.

questions.question: A student claims: for an open network, $\boldsymbol{I}-\boldsymbol{P}$ is invertible, so that the traffic equations have a unique solution, only if every station has a positive exit probability $P_{i0}>0$. Which assessment of this claim is correct?
options: Correct: a station with $P_{i0}=0$ keeps its jobs inside, so no unique solution exists.
Wrong: a tandem line fed at station 1 has $P_{i0}=0$ for $i<M$, yet $\lambda_i=\gamma_1$ uniquely.
Wrong: $\boldsymbol{I}-\boldsymbol{P}$ is always invertible, as every entry of $\boldsymbol{P}$ lies in $[0,1]$.
Wrong: what is needed instead is $P_{ii}=0$ at every station, so no job returns at once.

questions.question: A two-station tandem line receives jobs at station 1 at rate $\gamma_1=3$ per hour; every job goes on to station 2 and then leaves. Each station has one server and unlimited waiting room, with mean service times $\mathbb{E}[S_1]=0.4$ and $\mathbb{E}[S_2]=0.36$ hours. What is the long-run arrival rate at station 2?
options: 2.5 jobs per hour
3 jobs per hour
0.5 jobs per hour
$\tfrac{25}{9}\approx2.78$ jobs per hour

questions.question: In an open network, external jobs arrive only at station 1, at rate $\gamma$ per hour. After station 1 a job goes to station 2 with probability 0.5 or leaves; after station 2 it returns to station 1 with probability 0.5 or leaves. Single servers have $\mathbb{E}[S_1]=0.15$ and $\mathbb{E}[S_2]=0.5$ hours. Both loads are below one exactly when $\gamma<\gamma^*$. What is $\gamma^*$?
options: $\gamma^*=2$
$\gamma^*=5$
$\gamma^*=3$
